test_id resolution: manifest alias `case_070` -> style_id `linework_coloring_bold_outer_sparse_inner_limited_two_tone_soft_two_band_reflected_color_complete_line_color` -> scorecard rows P7000208 (seed 1001), P7000209 (seed 2002), P7000210 (seed 3003). All three 1024x1024 renders were opened full size plus 3x NEAREST pixel crops of the sleeve/silhouette regions.

The hold rested on two claims; both fail at full resolution.

1. "thin 1px uniform contour with no weight emphasis" is false. Horizontal scanline runs across the left sleeve silhouette of P7000208 give an outer contour 2-3 px wide with minimum luminance ~28-71, while the interior fold marks in the same rows are 1 px wide at ~99-161 luminance. That is a clear dual emphasis in both width and value, and it is visible directly in the 3x crops: a continuous near-black heavier silhouette line against thin light-grey interior hairlines. The same hierarchy holds in P7000209 and P7000210 (the cuff/sleeve edges in both are distinctly darker and heavier than any interior mark). A 2-3 px contour collapses to 1 px and loses its value separation from 1 px grey interior lines under contact-sheet downsampling, which is exactly the artifact the original note flagged as "below thumbnail resolution."

2. "moderately dense fold hatching rather than sparse interior" is seed-local, not the case. It is a fair description of P7000208 only. P7000209 and P7000210 both show a markedly clean, sparse sweater interior — a handful of delicate fold marks with large untouched areas. Even on P7000208 the interior marks are all thin light-grey, so the bold-outer/delicate-inner relationship the token specifies is intact; the density is at the high end of "sparse," not inverted.

Cross-checked against the three other cases sharing the identical coloring/shading/accent triple (case_020 angular_precise, case_122 crisp_uniform, case_201 fine_tapered): case_070 has the highest outer-to-inner width ratio of the four (mean ~1.89 vs 1.39-1.55), i.e. the bold-outer emphasis is discriminative against the uniform-weight control rather than generic to the rig. A naive dark-run density metric ranked case_070's interior highest, but inspection shows that metric is counting soft_two_band shading edges rather than lines, so it is not evidence on sparseness.

Saturation was not the concern, but saturation_screen.json was checked for completeness: this item's palette group `limited_two_tone` (43 items, median 0.1378) reports outlier_count 0, so no colour evidence against it either.

Recommend clearing the hold to pass.
